text:
**Anonymous post for someone else: **

We did the citizenship interview and got invited to the loyalty declaration ceremony. By super bad luck, I simply cannot attend on that date, so they told me I will have to wait for whenever the next date will be. In theory that is fine, but in practice in the meantime I got accepted for a 1.5-year job abroad. Our long-term plans are to continue our life here, my partner will stay here and we will do long-distance for that time period, but this is an important professional opportunity for me that I can't give up (and the role will actually help my local career, that's a large part of why I want to do it). 

My question is, should I inform Misrad Hapnim upfront about this? Because whenever the next date will be for the loyalty ceremony, I will already have moved, and they will see that I have been abroad for some months. Will this raise questions about my commitment to live here and might they backtrack on their decision, and so is it better to clarify the reason upfront - or is it better not to do anything (because clarifying upfront could also cause them to backtrack), and only clarify if asked? Our intentions are genuine, and they've seen us every year for the past 8 years and things always go smoothly, but still I don't know how understanding they may be. [note if relevant: we are not married]
